Action Plan:
- Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.
- Suspected acute gastroenteritis (likely viral) with non-bloody diarrhea and central abdominal pain; initiate supportive care focused on hydration and avoidance of unnecessary antibiotics.
- Advise hydration optimization and dietary intake as tolerated; monitor for red flags (fever, dehydration, inability to keep fluids down, GI bleeding); return for in-person evaluation if red flags develop.
- Recommend staying home and limiting work until symptoms improve; if symptoms persist or worsen over the next couple of days, pursue an in-person GP visit for further assessment.
- Reassure regarding cancer concern given family history; if symptoms persist or new concerning signs arise, discuss with GP for appropriate workup.
- Document that no antibiotics were prescribed today; no planned imaging or labs at this time.
- If consultation quality requires, consider review of inhaler use and allergy status at next visit.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: 3 days of diarrhea with associated abdominal pain and vomiting.
- Onset/duration: Symptoms began ~3 days ago; ongoing.
- Symptom details:
  - Diarrhea: frequent, urgent bowel movements (described as often, roughly every 10 minutes at times); no visible blood in stool reported.
  - Abdominal pain: central (periumbilical) area; mild tenderness on palpation; may be associated with gas.
  - Vomiting: occurred this morning; no definite blood in vomit; vomiting stopped after short episode; appetite limited but some fruit intake earlier.
  - Hydration: uncertain fluid intake; potential mild dehydration risk.
- Triggers/relief: No clear food trigger; possible anxiety; symptoms persistent without clear improvement or worsening.
- Medical history: Asthma; uses inhaler.
- Medications: Inhaler for asthma; dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Allergies: NKDA (no known drug allergies) per patient.
- Social history: Not detailed.
- Family history: Father died of bowel cancer about 10 years ago; patient concerned about cancer risk.
- Review of systems: No reported fever; no chest pain; able to walk and talk; no blood observed in stool; no blood observed in vomit (though patient noted potential strawberries as cause for red hue, not blood).

Objective:
- General: Patient ambulatory, able to converse normally.
- Abdomen: Central abdominal pain with mild tenderness on palpation; no guarding or rebound described.
- GI: Diarrhea present; no blood in stool reported; vomiting occurred earlier in the day; able to tolerate some fruit earlier.
- Respiratory: Asthma history; no acute distress described; inhaler use noted.
- Cardiovascular/other: Not assessed or not documented.
- Vital signs: Not documented in the transcript.
- Investigations: None performed or ordered during this visit.

Assessment & Plan:
1) Acute gastroenteritis (likely viral) vs gastroenteritis of uncertain etiology:
   - Assessment: Acute gastroenteritis is the leading working diagnosis based on 3 days of non-bloody diarrhea, central abdominal pain, vomiting, and lack of red-flag systemic symptoms.
   - Differential diagnosis (consistent with transcript and DDx):
     - Acute viral gastroenteritis (high likelihood per DDx)
     - Acute bacterial gastroenteritis / food poisoning (medium likelihood)
     - IBD flare (low to medium likelihood)
     - Colorectal cancer given family history (low likelihood for this acute presentation)
     - Lactose intolerance/malabsorption (possible contributing factor)
     - Drug-induced GI upset from new inhaler (low likelihood)
     - Other intra-abdominal processes (e.g., appendicitis) considered low likelihood given presentation
   - Investigations: None planned at this time; no labs/imaging ordered unless symptoms worsen.
   - Treatment: Supportive care only
     - Hydration: Encourage increased oral fluid intake with hydration strategies (oral rehydration solutions as appropriate).
     - Diet: Light, easily digestible foods as tolerated; avoid heavy meals while symptomatic.
     - Antibiotics: Not recommended at this time based on current presentation and clinician guidance.
     - Monitoring: Self-monitor for fever, dehydration, persistent vomiting, or GI bleeding; return to care if symptoms worsen.
   - Referrals: None at this time; if symptoms persist or worsen, in-person GP evaluation advised.

Quality checks (document_quality):
- Missing elements: Vitals and targeted physical exam details (no vitals documented); explicit medication dosing for current inhaler not provided; detailed allergy history beyond NKDA; social history limited.
- Internal conflicts: None identified between transcript and DDx notes; consistent with plan.
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor repetition and filler words present; no missing critical data impacting the clinical plan.
